title: Cylinder 1 Injector Circuit High
shortDescription: Cylinder 1 fuel injector circuit reports high voltage.
fullDescription: The PCM has detected a fault on the fuel injector circuit for cylinder 1, specifically high voltage. This typically indicates damaged injector wiring, a failed injector coil, or a PCM driver stage fault. The cylinder may be cut from operation to protect the catalytic converter.
safetyImpact: Misfire and reduced power; potential catalytic converter damage if driven extensively.

causes.cause: Low compression or mechanical issue on the cylinder

symptoms: Check Engine Light (often flashing under load)

fixSteps.title: Confirm Code and Misfire Counts
fixSteps.instruction: Use a scan tool with live data to verify cylinder-specific misfire counts and freeze-frame conditions.

fixSteps.title: Swap Injector to Confirm
fixSteps.instruction: Swap the cylinder 1 injector with one from a known-good cylinder. Clear codes and drive. If the fault follows the injector, replace it.

fixSteps.title: Test Injector Circuit
fixSteps.instruction: Measure injector coil resistance and check the harness for continuity, shorts, and proper PCM driver pulse with a noid light or scope.

fixSteps.title: Replace Injector and Reset
fixSteps.instruction: Install a new OEM-quality injector with new seals. Clear codes, perform any required injector coding, and road-test.

faq.q: Can I drive with this code?
faq.a: Avoid driving long distances. Continued misfire can damage the catalytic converter and oxygen sensors.

faq.q: Do I need to replace all injectors?
faq.a: Not necessarily. If injectors are old and high mileage, replacing as a set can be wise to avoid further failures.

faq.q: Will the injector need coding after replacement?
faq.a: On many modern direct-injection engines, yes. The injector flow code must be entered with a scan tool to ensure precise fueling.
